text.tspan: With Svija, you can finally use
all the power of modern design tools
on the internet.
All the techniques of professional graphic design are now possible online. They all
work natively, completely integrated in the web page.
Until now, internet content has had little to do with other content. Publishing an ad
campaign on line has involved creating a few (mediocre) images, and embedding them
in a mediocre web page.
Svija, by using the same tools that professional designers use in other domains, now
makes it possible to share content freely between print and electronic media.
You can create a gorgeous web site from your brochure files in a matter of minutes, or
turn your film poster into a launch-party website, or any number of other things.
The limits of HTML and browser
technology have restricted websites to:

g.text: Everything else you see is approximated using these basic tools.
Until now, the internet has been a second-class citizen
Until now, the internet been isolated, cut off from civilization
Svija ends the separation between the internet and real graphic design.
These techniques are not only possible, they're easy:

text.tspan: People appreciate good design.
They hang movie posters and advertising
on their wall,
because it's beautiful
But how often have you wanted to
make a
poster of your website?
Svija will change that.
This illustration is not a
separate image — it's part
of the page!
• overflowing and overlapping objects
• twisted or distorted objects
• continuity across an entire page
• free-form elements
• curves
• transparency
• angled objects
• gradients
There are some techiques available in Adobe Illustrator that do not translate directly to the SVG format.
These include mostly effects that mimic Photoshop filters.

g.text: websites are all just rows of rectangles, rows of rectangles, rows of… yawn.

text.tspan: • SMALL
• BORING
• SLOW
After
visiting
an SVG-based website, visiting an HTML-based website feels:
Exact Content Placement
uses exact coordinates to place every element on the page.
ECP permits a level of detail and precision that was not previously available to website builders.
Whereas HTML-based websites are subject to imprecision from several sources (window site, browser, OS
etc.), ECP-based websites are exact. The content is perfect, every time.
It's finally worth the effort to make a perfect website.
When you edit a page you aren't limited to changing one picture, or swapping out a block of
text — all the content is totally accessible. This illustration is
in
the page, just as much as the
other text:
because the content is now part of the page, you can edit and work on the page much more
directly — that little hand in the footer is IN the footer — it's not a placed image. When I
designed the footer, I could move and adjust the hand freely without having to re-import an
image each time.
since everything is so precise, it's suddenly worthwhile to pay attention to alignment, to make
the page pixel-perfect.
the content is fully integrated into the page, not just placed in little boxes
a regular website is alternating images and text
A svija site has content integrated in the page. It's beautiful.
